page: Vultr vhf-6c-24gb is a virtual machine belonging to the High Frequency Compute family, configured with 6 shared x86_64 vCPUs derived from 3 physical Intel cores with multithreading running at 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 4 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache, with support for standard hardware instruction sets including AVX, AES, FMA, and BMI2. The instance provides 24.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. No discrete GPU acceleration is present. Local high-speed persistence is bundled via a 448 GB NVMe SSD, and the configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark analysis demonstrates middle-tier baseline compute capabilities across synthetic and real-world metrics. In stress-ng, the configuration scores 1670.29 in single-core and 9438.87 in multi-core throughput, complemented by Geekbench scores of 1612.0 single-core and 6307.0 multi-core. Single-threaded gzip compression performs in the upper quartile at 33.56 GB/sec, and Geekbench text processing shows strong results at 2575.0 points. Cached memory bandwidth reaches 674.29 GB/sec; however, uncached memory writes drop to 13.1 GB/sec, placing it in the lower tiers for sustained heavy memory streaming. PassMark tests confirm intermediate results across standard integer and extended instructions, though physics calculations and database operations demonstrate weaker relative figures.

Given its shared CPU allocation paired with bundled fast NVMe storage and balanced memory, the instance delivers practical resource density without the cost profile of dedicated hardware. Workload fit includes medium-scale web application serving, CI/CD compilation runners, software build pipelines, staging environments, and caching services such as Redis where the recorded throughput of 7.25 million operations per second satisfies moderate operational requirements.
